title: Exact distances of eight PRIDE linear-layer code instances
summary: Determine the exact maximum minimum distance for eight linear-code instances used to bound PRIDE branch numbers.

formal_statement.body: For each of the eight pairs $(b,n)\in\{(2,11),(2,16),(3,11),(3,12),(3,13),(3,14),(3,15),(3,16)\}$, determine the exact maximum Hamming minimum distance $d_{\max}([2n,n]_{\mathbb F_{2^b}})$. Equivalently, collapse the source intervals $8\text{--}9$, $11\text{--}12$, $9\text{--}10$, $10\text{--}11$, $10\text{--}12$, $11\text{--}13$, $11\text{--}14$, and $12\text{--}15$ to their exact integer optima by giving matching constructions and upper bounds. These distances determine attainable linear and differential branch-number bounds for the corresponding SPN linear layers.

scope.domain: Linear [2n,n] codes over $\mathbb F_{2^b}$ used as the coding-theoretic model for symmetric block-cipher linear layers
assumptions: Code length is $2n$ and dimension is $n$.
The objective is Hamming minimum distance, identified by the source with the branch-number objective for its linear layers.
The eight finite parameter instances are audited pointwise.
scope.unresolved_remainder: All eight instances remain interval-valued in the inspected Grassl code tables: F_4,[22,11] has 8-9; F_4,[32,16] has 11-12; F_8,[22,11] has 9-10; F_8,[24,12] has 10-11; F_8,[26,13] has 10-12; F_8,[28,14] has 11-13; F_8,[30,15] has 11-14; and F_8,[32,16] has 12-15.

provenance.note: The CRYPTO 2014 paper cites Grassl's online code tables for the intervals, but the earliest text-confirmed formulation of this exact cryptographic family has not been established.

progress.summary: The CRYPTO 2014 source records eight F_4 and F_8 linear-code instances whose best-known minimum-distance bounds are not exact and ties the distance to PRIDE branch-number design.
